tagline: From Havana over the top of Arkansas to Paris.
intro: Highway 309 leaves Highway 10 at Havana and climbs north through the Ozark National Forest onto Mount Magazine, a flat-topped mountain rimmed by cliffs whose Signal Hill, at 2,753 feet, is the highest point in Arkansas. An overlook along the way looks out over Blue Mountain Lake. Then the road comes down more than 2,300 feet, past Cove Lake, to Paris and on to Webb City, 45 miles in all.

The road itself is Depression work, built by the WPA and the Civilian Conservation Corps along with the trails and the dam at Cove Lake. The French named the mountain for a storehouse it was thought to resemble.

moments.title: Mount Magazine
moments.text: A sandstone-capped plateau spared by erosion and rimmed with sheer cliffs, where the Resettlement Administration bought out every private holding in 1934 and a state park now holds the top.

moments.title: Cove Lake Spillway Dam-Bridge
moments.text: The highway crosses the spillway on a five-arch masonry bridge, built with the earth and stone dam in 1937 on WPA money.

moments.title: Paris
moments.text: A Logan County seat named for the French capital in 1874 and later a coal town, it keeps an Eiffel Tower Park, the tower doubling as a fountain, with the historic courthouse behind.

sources.label: Arkansas Tourism, Road Trip: The Scenic Byway Guide to Northwest Arkansas
